## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `status()` shortens the revision to 7 characters, but its docstring says it uses the same identifier as `history`, and `history`/`completed` use 12. As a result, the running status line shows a different revision ID from the other deployment output. This review read the full pinned diff, `app/display.py` and `tests/test_display.py` at the PR head. It did not run the tests. `attempt_label` is correct and its test asserts exact output.

## Changes
Adds `status(revision, attempt)` and `attempt_label(attempt)` to `app/display.py`, which build a "Running: <revision> (attempt N)" line. Also adds tests for both functions in `tests/test_display.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — Use `revision[:12]` in `status()` to match history — For `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef..."`, `status(REVISION, 2)` returns `"Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)"`, while `history` and `completed` (lines 5 and 9) print `0123456789ab`. The docstring at line 13 says "Show the deployment revision using the same identifier as history.", so the code contradicts its stated contract. The added test at tests/test_display.py:14-15 checks only the prefix and suffix, so it passes with either length. — Operators comparing the running status with history and completion output see two different identifiers for the same deployment, and no test catches the mismatch. — Fix: Change the slice to `revision[:12]` (or share one helper with `history`/`completed`), and assert the full string in the test: `status(REVISION, 2) == "Running: 0123456789ab (attempt 2)"`.
